title: Environment, volumes and profiles
summary: Variable substitution and .env files, env_file, named volumes, and optional services with profiles.

steps.title: Two different .env ideas
body: Compose has two features that both involve "env files" and are easy to confuse:
**1. Interpolation** — `${VAR}` in `compose.yaml` is replaced by Compose *before anything runs*, from your shell's environment or a file named **`.env`** next to the compose file:
image: postgres:${PG_VERSION:-17}          # 17 unless PG_VERSION is set
POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?set DB_PASSWORD in .env}   # error if missing
- ./api.env          # each KEY=value line becomes a container env var
So `.env` configures **the compose file**; `env_file` configures **the container**. Keep `.env` out of git when it holds secrets, and commit a `.env.example` instead.

steps.prompt: `.env` contains `API_KEY=abc`. The compose file never mentions `API_KEY`. Does the api container see `API_KEY`?
options: No: `.env` only feeds `${...}` interpolation in the compose file
Yes: every container gets all variables from `.env`
steps.explain: To pass it in, write `environment: API_KEY: ${API_KEY}`, or put it in a file referenced by `env_file:`.

steps.prompt: Match each interpolation form to its behaviour.
pairs: the value of TAG, or empty (with a warning) if unset
TAG if set and non-empty, otherwise `dev`
fails with the message if TAG is unset or empty
a literal `$HOME`, passed on to the container's shell

steps.prompt: `.env` contains `PG_VERSION=16`. What image does Compose use for this service?
steps.explain: The default after `:-` only applies when the variable is unset or empty. Run `docker compose config` to see the fully interpolated file.

steps.title: Named volumes and profiles
body: Named volumes are declared at the top level and referenced by services; Compose creates them as `<project>_<name>`:
**Profiles** make services optional. A service with `profiles:` starts only when one of its profiles is enabled (or when you name it explicitly):
docker compose up -d                     services without profiles only
docker compose --profile tools up -d     ... plus adminer

steps.prompt: With the file above plus `db` and `api` (no profiles), which services start on `docker compose --profile tools up -d`?
steps.explain: Services without profiles always start; profiled ones only when a matching profile is enabled.

steps.prompt: Declare and use a named volume for Redis data.
steps.explain: `./redisdata` would be a bind mount of a host folder; `redisdata` refers to the volume declared at the bottom.

steps.title: Configure it with .env, check with compose config
prompt: This terminal has a **real Docker Engine** with Compose. `~/shop/compose.yaml` takes its settings from variables.
`cd ~/shop && docker compose config` fails until they are set.
Without editing `compose.yaml`, create `~/shop/.env` so that the API:
Check with `docker compose config`, then `docker compose up -d --wait`: `curl http://127.0.0.1:8081/` prints `api 1.1`.

checks.name: compose.yaml is unchanged
checks.fail: Leave `compose.yaml` as it is: the values belong in `.env`.

checks.name: compose config resolves the image, port and log level
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && docker compose config --format json | jq -r '[.services.api.image, (.services.api.ports[0] | "\(.host_ip):\(.published)"), .services.api.environment.LOG_LEVEL] | join(" ")'
checks.fail: `docker compose config` does not resolve to `shop/api:1.1`, `127.0.0.1:8081` and `debug`. Set `API_TAG`, `API_PORT` and `LOG_LEVEL` in `~/shop/.env`.

checks.name: the API answers on 127.0.0.1:8081
checks.fail: `curl http://127.0.0.1:8081/` does not print `api 1.1`. Did `docker compose up -d --wait` run?

hints: Compose reads `.env` next to `compose.yaml` for `${...}` substitution: one `NAME=value` per line.
`${API_TAG:-1.0}` uses 1.0 only when `API_TAG` is unset or empty; `${API_PORT:?...}` stops with that message when it is.
`printf '%s\n' API_TAG=1.1 API_PORT=8081 LOG_LEVEL=debug > ~/shop/.env`, then `docker compose config`.
steps.explain: `${VAR:-default}` and `${VAR:?message}` let one compose file serve every environment while failing fast when something required is missing. `.env` is read for substitution only; the values reach a container only where the file uses them (`environment:` here). `docker compose config` shows the resolved result, which is how you debug "why is it using the wrong tag?".

steps.title: Optional services with profiles
prompt: This terminal has a **real Docker Engine** with Compose. `~/shop/compose.yaml` has the everyday services `web` and
`cache`, a `debug` toolbox in the `debug` profile, and a one-off `seed` job in the `tools` profile.
1. start the everyday services **and** the debug toolbox, but not `seed`;
2. run `seed` **once**, so it fills its volume, and leave no `seed` container behind.

checks.name: web, cache and debug run; seed does not
checks.fail: Running services should be `cache`, `debug` and `web`. `debug` only starts with its profile: `docker compose --profile debug up -d`.

checks.name: seed ran once and finished
checks.fail: The `seed` tool has not run. A one-off run of a service: `docker compose run --rm seed`.

checks.name: no seed container is left behind
checks.fail: A `seed` container is still there. `--rm` removes it when it finishes.

hints: Services with `profiles:` start only when one of their profiles is enabled: `--profile NAME` (or `COMPOSE_PROFILES`).
Naming a service on the command line runs it whatever its profile.
`docker compose --profile debug up -d`, then `docker compose run --rm seed`.
steps.explain: Profiles keep one compose file for the whole team without starting everything for everyone: debug tools, admin UIs and one-off jobs stay off until asked for. `docker compose run --rm` is the way to run a job service once (migrations, seeds), with the project's networks and volumes but without leaving a container behind.
